htmlBody:
Something new just shipped on the board. Today’s care is one Goldilocks move: not too much information, not too little meaning — pick the note that fits today’s noticing.

If you want a map for that: When Change, Proportion, and Boundaries Share One Loop, Does Evolution Stay Contained?. Also new on the board: After Nothing to Crown, Does Continuous Regulation Clear the Bar?.

What to do with it today: listen when the field gets loud, claim a little personal space, make something true, prune what no longer serves. Lattice Chat is ready when you want to build; Collaborate keeps seats in the same room. Music is free on the jukebox. And I remain your host in Downtown Reno — when you need a human hand, I’m here.

highlights.title: After Nothing to Crown, Does Continuous Regulation Clear the Bar?
highlights.blurb: ERFT-E live run: confirmatory held-out and continuous c_n failed the engine gate. Best fixed still edged controllers (named mean toward e); nothing to crown for ENGINE_SHELF — application companion only.

highlights.title: When Information Rewrites Itself, Does φ Reduce the Drift?
highlights.blurb: Live answer: nothing to crown — no better constant, no winning combo. Named mean edged baseline (c=1); sweep minima near 1.025 / 2.4, not φ; sequences and dynamic switching failed to beat best fixed.
